cues.en: About 10 years ago, I took on the task to teach global development to Swedish undergraduate students. That was after having spent about 20 years together with African institutions studying hunger in Africa. So I was sort of expected to know a little about the world.
cues.zh: 大约十年前，我接下了一个任务，给瑞典的本科生讲授全球发展。在那之前，我已经和非洲的科研机构一起研究了20年的非洲饥荒。所以大家理所当然地觉得，我对这个世界多多少少有些了解。

cues.en: I started in our medical university, Karolinska Institute, an undergraduate course called Global Health. But when you get that opportunity, you get a little nervous. I thought these students coming to us actually have the highest grade you can get in Swedish college systems. So I thought maybe they know everything I'm going to teach them about. So I did a pre-test when they came. And one of the questions from which I learned a lot was this one. Which country has the highest child mortality of these five pairs?
cues.zh: 我在我们医科大学 Karolinska Institute 开设了一门名为“全球健康”的本科课程。但真拿到这个机会时，心里其实有点发怵。我想，能进我们学校的都是瑞典高等教育体系里考分最高的学生。我觉得他们可能早就知道我要讲的一切了。所以他们入学时我做了个摸底测验。其中有一道题让我受益匪浅，就是这道：在这五组国家中，哪一个的儿童死亡率更高？

cues.en: And I put them together so that in each pair of country, one has twice the child mortality of the other. And this means that it's much bigger the difference than the uncertainty of the data.
cues.zh: 我特意把它们两两配对，让每组中一个国家的儿童死亡率是另一个的两倍。这意味着两者差距足够大，远超数据本身的不确定性误差。

cues.en: I won't put you at a test here, but it's Turkey, which is highest there, Poland, Russia, Pakistan, and South Africa, and these were the results of the Swedish students. I did it, so I got a confidence interval, which was pretty narrow, and I got happy, of course, at 1.8 right answer out of five possible. That means that there was a place for a professor of international health and for my course. But one late night, when I was compiling the report, I really realized my discovery.
cues.zh: 我这里就不考大家了，死亡率更高的分别是土耳其、波兰、俄罗斯、巴基斯坦和南非，而这就是瑞典学生的测试结果。我计算了一下，得到了一个非常窄的置信区间；满分5分他们平均只答对1.8道，我当然挺高兴的。这说明我这个国际健康学教授没有失业，我的课很有必要。但直到深夜整理报告时，我才真正意识到自己的发现有多惊人。

cues.en: I have shown that Swedish top students know statistically significantly less about the world than the chimpanzees. Because the chimpanzee would score half right. If I gave them two bananas with Sri Lanka and Turkey, they would be right, half of the cases. But the students are not there. The problem for me was not ignorance, it was preconceived ideas. I did also an unethical study of the professors of the Karolinska Institute.
cues.zh: 我证明了：瑞典顶尖大学生对世界的认知，在统计学意义上显著落后于大猩猩。因为让大猩猩来选，至少能猜对一半。如果我给它们两根分别标着斯里兰卡和土耳其的香蕉，它们猜对的概率也有50%。但学生们甚至不如大猩猩。我发现问题不在于无知，而在于先入为主的偏见。后来我还对 Karolinska Institute 的教授们做了一次“不太道德”的测试——

cues.en: that hands out the Nobel Prize in medicine and they are on par with the chimpanzee there. So this is where I realized that there was really a need to communicate because the data of what's happening in the world and the child health of every country is very well aware. So we did the software which displays it like this. Every bubble here is a country. This country over here, this is China.
cues.zh: 那可是负责评选诺贝尔生理学或医学奖的机构，结果他们的水平也就和大猩猩打个平手。这让我意识到，普及真实认知有多迫切，因为世界的发展现状和各国的儿童健康数据其实都是公开透明的。于是我们做了一款软件，像这样来直观呈现。这里的每个气泡都代表一个国家。这边的这个国家，就是中国。

cues.en: And this is India. The size of the bubble is the population. And on this axis here, I put fertility rate. Because my students, what they said when they looked upon the world, and I asked them, what do you really think about the world? Well, I first discovered that the textbook was tinting mainly. And they said, the world is still we and them. And we is Western world, and them is third world.
cues.zh: 这是印度。气泡的大小代表人口规模。在这边的坐标轴上，我放的是生育率。因为每当我问学生：“你们到底是怎么看这个世界的？”我首先发现教科书本身就带着严重偏见。他们回答说，世界依然分为“我们”和“他们”：“我们”是西方世界，而“他们”是第三世界。

cues.en: And what do you mean with Western world? I said, well, that's long life in small family, and third world is short life in large family. So this is what I could display here.
cues.zh: 你说的“西方世界”是什么意思？我说，嗯，那就是小家庭、长寿命；而第三世界是大家庭、短寿命。所以这就是我能在这里展示的。

cues.en: I put fertility rate here, number of children per woman, one, two, three, four, up to about eight children per woman. We have very good data since 1962, 1960, about on the size of families in all countries. The arrow margin is narrow. Here I put life expectancy at birth from 30 years in some countries up to about 70 years. And 1962, there was really a group of countries here that was industrialized countries and they had...
cues.zh: 我把生育率放在这里，每名妇女生育的孩子数，一、二、三、四，直到大约八个孩子。我们有1962年、1960年以来非常好的数据，关于所有国家的家庭规模。箭头边距很窄。这里我放的是出生时预期寿命，从一些国家的30岁到大约70岁。而1962年，这里确实有一组国家，是工业化国家，它们有……

cues.en: small families and long lives. And these were the developing countries. They had large families and they had relatively short lives. Now, what has happened since 1962? We want to see the change. Are the students right? It's still two types of countries. Or have these developing countries got smaller families and they live here? Or have they got longer lives and live up there? Let's see. We stopped the world. And this is all UN statistic that has been available. Here we go. Can you see that? It's China. They're moving against better health. They're improving their...
cues.zh: 小家庭和长寿命。而这些是发展中国家。它们有大家庭，寿命相对较短。那么，1962年以来发生了什么？我们想看看变化。学生们说得对吗？仍然有两类国家。还是这些发展中国家变成了更小的家庭，住到了这里？还是它们寿命变长，住到了上面？我们来看看。我们把世界停住了。这些都是可获得的联合国统计数据。开始了。你能看到吗？这是中国。它们正朝着更好的健康水平移动。它们在改善自己的……

cues.en: of the green Latin American countries. They are moving towards smaller families. The yellow ones here are the Arabic countries, and they get larger families, longer lives, but not larger families. The Africans are the green down here. They still remain here. This is India. Indonesia is moving on pretty fast. And in the 80s here, you have Bangladesh still among the African countries there. But not Bangladesh. It's a miracle that happens in the 80s. The imams start to promote family planning. And they move up into that corner. And in the 90s, we have the terrible.
cues.zh: 绿色的拉丁美洲国家。它们正走向更小的家庭。这里黄色的是阿拉伯国家，它们的家庭更大、寿命更长，但家庭规模没有变得更大。非洲国家是下面这些绿色的。它们仍然留在这里。这是印度。印度尼西亚前进得相当快。而在80年代这里，孟加拉国还在非洲国家那一群里。但不是孟加拉国。这是80年代发生的奇迹。伊玛目开始推广计划生育。于是它们向上移动到那个角落。而到了90年代，我们遇到了可怕的

cues.en: HIV epidemic that takes down the life expectancy of the African countries and all the rest of the world moves up into the corner where we have long lives and small family and we have a completely new world. Let me make a comparison directly between United States of America and Vietnam. 1964. America had small families and long life. Vietnam had large families and short lives. And this is what happens. The data during the war
cues.zh: HIV疫情，它拉低了非洲国家的预期寿命，而世界其他地区则向上移动到那个角落——长寿和小家庭——于是我们有了一个全新的世界。让我直接比较美国和越南。1964年。美国是小家庭、长寿命。越南是大家庭、短寿命。接下来发生的是这样。战争期间的数据

cues.en: indicate that even with all the death there was an improvement of life expectancy. By the end of the year the family planning started in Vietnam and they went for smaller families and the United States up there is getting for longer life keeping family size and in the eighties now they give up communist planning and they go for market economy and it moves faster even in social life and today we have in Vietnam the same life expectancy and the same family size
cues.zh: 表明，即使有那么多死亡，预期寿命仍有所改善。到那年年底，越南开始了计划生育，他们转向更小的家庭；而上面的美国在保持家庭规模的同时寿命变长。到了80年代，他们放弃共产主义计划经济，转向市场经济，连社会生活也变化得更快；今天越南的预期寿命和家庭规模

cues.en: here in Vietnam in 2003, as in the United States in 1974 by the end of the war. I think we all, if we don't look in the data, we underestimate the tremendous change in Asia, which was in social change before we saw the economical change. So let's move over to another way here in which we could display the distribution in the world of the income. This is the world distribution of income.
cues.zh: 在2003年的越南，和1974年战争结束时的美国一样。我想，如果我们不看数据，就会低估亚洲的巨大变化；这种变化先是社会变化，然后我们才看到经济变化。所以让我们换一种方式，来展示世界收入分布。这就是世界收入分布。

cues.en: of people, $1, $10, or $100 per day. There's no gap between rich and poor any longer. This is a myth. There's a little hump here. But there are people all the way. And if we look where the income ends up, the income, this is 100% of world's annual income. And the rich is 20%. They take out of that about 74%.
cues.zh: 按人算，每天1美元、10美元或100美元。贫富之间不再有鸿沟。这是个迷思。这里有个小小的隆起。但各个收入段都有人。如果看收入最终落在哪里，这是全球年收入的100%。富人占20%。他们拿走其中约74%。

cues.en: And the poorest 20%, they take about 2%. And this shows that the concept of developing countries is extremely doubtful. We sort of think about aid, like these people here, giving aid to these people here. But in the middle, we have most of the world population, and they have now 24% of the income. We heard it in other forums. And who are these? Where are the different countries? I can show you Africa.
cues.zh: 最穷的20%只拿到约2%。这说明发展中国家的概念非常可疑。我们总想着援助，就像这边的人援助那边的人。但中间有世界上大多数人口，他们现在占收入的24%。我们在其他论坛听过。这些人是谁？不同国家在哪里？我给你们看看非洲。

cues.en: Africa. 10% of world population, most in poverty. This is OECD, the rich country, the country club of the UN. And they are over here on this side, and quite an overlap between Africa and OECD. And this is Latin America. It has everything on this earth, from the poorest to the richest in Latin America. And on top of that, we can put East Europe.
cues.zh: 非洲。占世界人口10%，多数处于贫困。这是OECD，富国，联合国的富国俱乐部。他们在这边，非洲和OECD重叠相当多。这是拉丁美洲。它拥有世间一切，从拉丁美洲最穷到最富。此外，我们还可以放上东欧。

cues.en: We can put East Asia and we could South Asia. And how did it look like if we go back in time to about 1970? Then there was more of a hump. And we have most who lived in absolute poverty were Asians. The problem in the world was the poverty in Asia. And if I now...
cues.zh: 我们可以放上东亚，还可以放上南亚。如果回到1970年左右，那时是什么样子？那时隆起更明显。绝对贫困人口大多数是亚洲人。当时世界的问题就是亚洲的贫困。而现在如果我……

cues.en: Let the world move forward. You will see that while population increase, there are hundreds of millions in Asia getting out of poverty and some others get into poverty. And this is the pattern we have today. And the best projection from the World Bank is that this will happen. And we will not have a divided world. We will have most people in the middle. Of course it's a logarithmic scale here. But our concept of economy is growth with percent. We look upon it as a possibility of...
cues.zh: 让世界向前发展。你会看到，随着人口增长，亚洲有数亿人摆脱贫困，另一些人则陷入贫困。这就是我们今天的模式。世界银行最好的预测是这将会发生。我们将不会有一个分裂的世界。大多数人会处在中间。当然这里是对数刻度。但我们的经济概念是按百分比增长。我们把它看作一种……的可能性。

cues.en: If I change this and I take GDP per capita instead of family income and I turn this individual
cues.zh: 如果我把这个改一下，用人均GDP而不是家庭收入，并把这个个体

cues.en: data into regional data of gross domestic products and I take the regions down here, the size of the bubble is still the population and you have the OECD there and you have Sub-Saharan Africa there and we take off the Arab states there coming both from Africa and from Asia and we put them separately and we can expand this axis and I can give it a new dimension here by adding the social values there, child survival. Now I have money on that axis and I have the possibility of children
cues.zh: 数据转成各地区国内生产总值数据，我取下面这些地区，气泡大小仍然表示人口，这里有OECD，这里有撒哈拉以南非洲，我们把来自非洲和亚洲的阿拉伯国家摘出来，单独放置，然后我们可以扩展这个坐标轴，并通过加入社会价值——儿童存活率——给它增加一个新维度。现在那个轴上是钱，我还可以看儿童

cues.en: to survive there. In some countries, 99.7% of children survive to five years of age, others only 70. And here it seems that there is a gap between OECD, Latin America, East Europe, East Asia, Arab states, South Asia, and Sub-Saharan Africa. The linearity is very strong between child survival and money. But let me split Sub-Saharan Africa. He else is there.
cues.zh: 能否存活下来。在一些国家，99.7%的儿童能活到五岁，另一些国家只有70%。这里似乎OECD、拉丁美洲、东欧、东亚、阿拉伯国家、南亚和撒哈拉以南非洲之间存在差距。儿童存活率和金钱之间的线性关系非常强。但让我把撒哈拉以南非洲拆开。还有什么呢？

cues.en: Health is up there. I can go here and I can split sub-Saharan Africa into its countries. And when it bursts, the size of each country bubble is the size of the population. Sierra Leone down there, Mauritius up there. Mauritius was the first country to get away with trade barriers and they could sell their sugar, they could sell their textiles on equal terms as the people in Europe and North America. There's a huge difference between Africa and Ghana is here in the middle.
cues.zh: 健康指标在上面。我点到这里，把撒哈拉以南非洲拆分成各个国家。散开后，每个国家气泡的大小就代表人口规模。塞拉利昂在下面，毛里求斯在上面。毛里求斯是第一个摆脱贸易壁垒的国家，他们能和欧美以同等条件销售食糖和纺织品。非洲各国之间差异巨大，加纳就在中间位置。

cues.en: In Sierra Leone, a humanitarian aid. Here in Uganda, development aid. Here, time to invest. There you can go for holiday. It's a tremendous variation within Africa, which we very often make, that it's equal everything. I can split South Asia here. India is the big bubble in the middle, but huge difference between Afghanistan and Sri Lanka. And I can split Arab states. How are they? Same climate.
cues.zh: 在塞拉利昂，需要的是人道主义援助。在乌干达，则是发展援助。在这里，适合投资。去那里，你可以去度假。非洲内部存在巨大差异，而我们却常常一概而论，以为那里的一切都一样。我可以把南亚拆开。印度是中间那个大气泡，但阿富汗和斯里兰卡差异悬殊。我再拆开阿拉伯国家。它们怎么样？气候一样。

cues.en: Same culture, same religion, huge difference. Even between neighbors, Yemen Civil War, United Arab Emirates money, which was quite equally and well used. Not as the myth is. And that includes all the children of the foreign workers who are in the country. Data is often better than you think. Many people say data is bad. There is an uncertainty margin. But we can see the difference here, Cambodia, Singapore. The differences are much bigger than the weakness of the data. East Europe,
cues.zh: 文化相同，宗教相同，差距却极大。即使是邻国之间——也门深陷内战，而 United Arab Emirates 非常富裕，且资金分配得当、使用合理。并不像传闻说的那样。这还包括了该国所有外籍劳工的子女。数据往往比你想象的更准确。很多人说数据不好，存在不确定区间。但我们能看到这里的差异，比如柬埔寨和新加坡。这些实际差距远大于数据的误差。再看东欧，

cues.en: Soviet economy for a long time, but they come out after 10 years very, very differently. And there is Latin America. Today we don't have to go to Cuba to find a healthy country in Latin America. Chile will have a lower child mortality than Cuba within some few years from now. And here we have high-income countries in OECD, and we get the whole pattern here of the world, which is more or less like this. And if we look at it...
cues.zh: 经历了长期的苏联经济体制，但10年后它们的发展路径截然不同。还有拉丁美洲。如今在拉美，我们不必去古巴才能找到健康的国家。几年之内，智利的儿童死亡率就会低于古巴。这里是 OECD 的高收入国家，于是我们就看到了世界的大致格局，基本就是这个样子。如果我们回过头看……

cues.en: how it looks to the world in 1960. It starts to move, 1960. This is Mao Zedong. He brought health to China. And then he died. And then Deng Xiaoping came and brought money to China and brought them into the mainstream again. And we have seen how countries move in different directions like this. So it's sort of difficult to get an example country which shows the pattern of the world. But I would like to bring you back to about here,
cues.zh: 看看1960年的世界是什么样。时间开始流动，1960年。这是 Mao Zedong。他给中国带来了健康。后来他去世了。接着 Deng Xiaoping 带来财富，让中国重新融入主流世界。我们看到各国就是这样朝不同方向演进的。所以很难找出一个代表性国家来展现全球格局。不过我想带大家回到大约这里，

cues.en: at 1960. And I would like to compare South Korea, which is this one, with Brazil, which is this one. The label went away for me here. And I would like to compare Uganda, which is there. And I can run it forward like this. And you can see how...
cues.zh: 回到1960年。我想对比一下韩国（这一个）和巴西（这一个）。这里的标签刚才跳掉了。我还想对比那边的乌干达。我可以像这样向前播放时间轴。大家可以看到……

cues.en: South Korea is making a very, very fast advancement, whereas Brazil is much slower. And if we move back again here and we put on trails on them like this, you can see again that the speed of development is very, very different. And the countries are moving more or less in the same rate
cues.zh: 韩国的进步非常非常快，而巴西则慢得多。如果我们再退回到这里，像这样给它们加上运动轨迹，大家会再次看到，两者的发展速度截然不同。各国基本都在以大致相仿的速率前进，

cues.en: as money and health. But it seems you can move much faster if you are healthy first than if you are wealthy first. And to show that you can put on the way of United Arab Emirates. They came from here, a mineral country. They catch all the oil, they got all the money, but health cannot be bought at the supermarket.
cues.zh: 同步积累财富与健康。但看起来，先拥有健康似乎比先拥有财富能让你发展得快得多。为了说明这点，可以看看 United Arab Emirates 的轨迹。他们从这里起步，一个资源型国家。他们抓住了石油红利，赚到了大笔财富，但健康是无法在超市里直接买到的。

cues.en: You have to invest in health. You have to get kids into schooling. You have to train health staff. You have to educate the population. And Shakespeare did that in a fairly good way. And in spite of falling oil prices, he brought this country up here. So we got a much more mainstream appearance of the world where all countries tend to use their money better than they used in the past. Now, this is more or less if you look at the average data of the countries.
cues.zh: 你必须投资健康。必须让孩子上学。必须培训卫生人员。必须教育民众。莎士比亚在这方面做得相当好。尽管油价下跌，他还是把这个国家带到了这里。于是我们看到世界呈现出更主流的面貌，所有国家都倾向于比过去更会用自己的钱。现在，如果你看各国的平均数据，情况大致就是这样。

cues.en: They are like this now that's dangerous to use average data because there's such a lot of difference within countries So if I go and look here we can see that Uganda that today is where South Korea was 1960 if I split Uganda There's quite a difference within Uganda These are the quintiles of Uganda the richest 20% of Ugandans are there the poorest are down there if I split South Africa
cues.zh: 现在它们就是这样。使用平均数据很危险，因为国家内部差异很大。所以如果我看这里，就能看到乌干达今天所处的位置，正是韩国1960年所处的位置。如果我把乌干达拆开，乌干达内部差异相当大。这些是乌干达的五分位：最富的20%乌干达人在这里，最穷的在下面。如果我把南非拆开

cues.en: It's like this. And if I go down and look at Nigeria, where there was such a terrible famine, lastly, it's like this. The 20% poorest of Niger is out here, and the 20% richest of South Africa is there, and yet we tend to discuss on what solutions there should be in Africa. Everything in this world exists in Africa.
cues.zh: 情况就是这样。再往下看尼日利亚，那里最近发生过如此严重的饥荒，情况就是这样。尼日尔最穷的20%在这里，南非最富的20%在那里，可我们却总在讨论非洲应该有什么解决方案。这个世界的一切都存在于非洲。

cues.en: And you can't discuss universal access to HIV for that quintile up here with the same strategy as down here. The improvement of the world must be highly contextualized and it's not relevant to have it on regional level. We must be much more detailed.
cues.zh: 你不能用下面那部分人的同样策略，来讨论上面这个五分位人群的HIV普遍可及性。世界的改善必须高度结合具体情境，放在地区层面并不合适。我们必须做得细致得多。

cues.en: We find that students get very excited when they can use this, and even more policymakers and the corporate sectors would like to see how the world is changing. Now, why doesn't this take place? Why are we not using the data we have? We have data in the United Nations, in the national statistical agencies, and in universities and other non-governmental organizations, because the data is hidden down in the databases, and the public is there, and the internet is there, but we have still not used it effectively.
cues.zh: 我们发现，学生能用上这个时会非常兴奋；政策制定者和企业界更想看到世界如何变化。那么，为什么这没有发生？为什么我们没在用已有的数据？我们在联合国、各国统计机构、大学和其他非政府组织里都有数据，因为数据被藏在数据库深处；公众在那里，互联网也在那里，但我们仍然没有有效利用它。

cues.en: All that information we saw changing in the world does not include publicly funded statistics. There are some web pages like this, you know? But they take some nourishment down from the databases, but people put prices on them. Stupid passwords and boring statistics. And this won't work. So what is needed? We have the databases. It's not a new database you need. We have wonderful design tools, and more and more are added up here.
cues.zh: 我们看到的世界变化的所有信息，并不包括公共资助的统计数据。有些网页像这样，你知道吗？它们从数据库里汲取养分，但人们给它们标价。烦人的密码和无聊的统计。这样行不通。那需要什么？我们有数据库。需要的不是新数据库。我们有很棒的设计工具，而且这里还在加入越来越多工具。

cues.en: So we started a non-profit venture, which we called linking data to design. We call it GapMinder from London Underground, where they warn you mind the gap. So we thought GapMinder was appropriate. And we started to write software which could link the data like this. And it wasn't that difficult. It took some person years. And we have produced animations. You can take a data set and put it there.
cues.zh: 所以我们创办了一个非营利项目，叫“将数据连接到设计”。我们把它叫做GapMinder，这个名字来自伦敦地铁，那里会提醒你“注意间隙”。所以我们觉得GapMinder很合适。我们开始写软件，能像这样连接数据。这并没有那么难。花了些人年。我们制作了动画。你可以取一个数据集放进去。

cues.en: We are liberating UN data, some few UN organisations, some countries accept that their databases can go out on the world. But what we really need is, of course, a search function. A search function where we can copy the data up to a searchable format and get it out in the world. And what do we hear when we go around? I've done anthropology on the main statistical units. Everyone says it's impossible.
cues.zh: 我们正在解放联合国数据，少数几个联合国机构、一些国家接受他们的数据库可以向全世界开放。但我们真正需要的当然是一个搜索功能。一个能把数据整理成可搜索格式并发布到全世界的搜索功能。我们四处走访时听到什么？我对主要统计单位做过人类学式调研。每个人都说这不可能。

cues.en: This can't be done. Our information is so peculiar and detailed, so that cannot be searched as others can be searched. We cannot give the data free to the students, free to the entrepreneurs of the world. But this is what we would like to see, isn't it?
cues.zh: 这做不到。我们的信息如此特殊、如此详细，没法像别的信息那样被搜索。我们不能把数据免费给学生，免费给全世界的创业者。但这正是我们想看到的，不是吗？

cues.en: The publicly funded data is down here and we would like flowers to grow out on the net and one of the crucial point is to make them searchable and then people can use the different design tool to animate it there. And I have a pretty good news for you. I have a good news that the present new head of UN statistic, he doesn't say it's impossible. He only says we can't do it. And that's a quite clever guy.
cues.zh: 公共资助的数据就在下面，我们希望网上能开出花来，关键之一就是让它们可被搜索，然后人们可以用各种设计工具把它做成动态展示。我有个好消息要告诉你们。好消息是，现任联合国统计负责人不说这不可能。他只说我们做不到。这家伙挺聪明的。

cues.en: We can see a lot happening in data in the coming years. We will be able to look at income distributions in completely new ways. This is the income distribution of China 1970. This is the income distribution of the United States 1970. Almost no overlap. Almost no overlap. And what has happened? What has happened is this. That China is growing. It's not so equal any longer. And it's appearing here.
cues.zh: 未来几年，我们能看到数据领域发生很多变化。我们将能以全新的方式看收入分布。这是1970年中国的收入分布。这是1970年美国的收入分布。几乎没有重叠。几乎没有重叠。后来发生了什么？发生的是这样：中国在增长。它不再那么平均了。它正出现在这里。

cues.en: overlooking the United States almost like a ghost, isn't it? It's pretty scary. But I think it's very important to have all this information. We need really to see it. And instead of looking at this, I would like to end up by showing the internet users per 1,000.
cues.zh: 几乎像幽灵一样俯视着美国，不是吗？挺吓人的。但我认为拥有所有这些信息非常重要。我们真的需要看到它。与其继续看这个，我想最后展示每千人互联网用户数。

cues.en: In this software, we access about 500 variables from all the countries quite easily. It takes some time to change for this. But on the axis, you can quite easily get any variable you would like to have. And the thing would be to get up the databases free, to get them searchable, and with a second click, to get them into the graphic formats where you can instantly
cues.zh: 在这个软件里，我们可以相当轻松地访问所有国家约500个变量。要切换到这种状态需要一些时间。但在坐标轴上，你可以很容易地调出任何想要的变量。关键是把数据库免费开放，让它们可被搜索，再点一下，就把它们转成图形格式，让你可以立刻

cues.en: Understand them now the statisticians doesn't like it because they say that this will not this will not Show The the reality we have to have statistical analytical methods, but this is hypothesis generating I end now with a world There the internet are coming the number of internet users are going up like this This is the GDP per capita and it's a new technology coming in but in the amazingly how well it fits
cues.zh: 理解它们。现在统计学家不喜欢这一点，因为他们说这不会——这不会展示现实，我们必须有统计分析方法；但这能生成假设。最后，我用一个世界来收尾：互联网正在到来，互联网用户数量像这样上升。这是人均GDP，而一项新技术正在进入，但令人惊讶的是它契合得多么好

cues.en: to the economy of the countries. That's why the $100 computer will be so important. But it's a nice tendency. It is as if the world is flattening off, isn't it? These countries are lifting more than the economy and will be very interesting to follow this over the year, as I would like you to be able to do with all the publicly funded data. Thank you very much. What if great ideas weren't cherished? What if they carried no importance? There is a place where artistic vision is protected.
cues.zh: 与各国的经济。这就是为什么100美元电脑会如此重要。但这是一个不错的趋势。就好像世界正在变平，不是吗？这些国家的提升不止于经济，未来一年跟踪这一趋势会非常有意思，我也希望你们能用所有公共资助数据做到这一点。非常感谢。如果伟大的想法不被珍视呢？如果它们无关紧要呢？有一个地方，艺术愿景受到保护。

cues.en: where inspired design ideas live on to become ultimate driving machines.
cues.zh: 灵感迸发的设计在此延续，最终成就极致驾驶机器。
